$Comment: The hunter waves of a chase round, run by the game's own encounter scripts. The round stands
this script up at the grove's centre the moment the hunt begins (the den roster is already out;
this file is what sends MORE hunters as the night gets worse) and takes it down with the round.
It never spawns a hunter itself: each rung below asks the round's hunter controller for one
wave through the KweebecHunterWave action, and the controller places the bodies, picks their
archetype off the round's own weighted, corruption-gated roster (Server/KweebecNightmare/Hunters),
paces them and counts them against the preset's live-hunter ceiling exactly as it does the den
roster, so a wave hunter is a hunter like any other.
The escalation is the five rungs under Hunt, each a Once sensor over ONE wave. Two read the
corruption tier through kweebecnightmare:corruption_tier (0 calm, 1 from a third of the meter, 2
from two thirds): the first fires when the tier reaches 1, the second when it reaches 2, each a
ring of hunters spaced evenly 18 blocks around the party's centre (Even true, AroundOnePlayer
false, Radius [18, 18]). Three read the cleansed-shrine count through
kweebecnightmare:shrines_lit and fire at the first, second and third shrine, each scattering
hunters between 8.4 and 14 blocks of ONE survivor picked at random (Even false, AroundOnePlayer
true) and telling the party the light drew them (Announce true). Count [1, 1] with PerPlayer
true is one hunter per party member per wave; the ceiling the preset's MaxHunters sets always
wins, so a wave that finds no room puts nobody down.
A rung is spent the moment it fires, so there is no cooldown and no per-round cap to tune: the
number of rungs IS the cap, and two shrines cleansed seconds apart draw two waves. Make the
hunt harder by adding a rung (a fourth shrine at Value [4, 99], a bigger Count, a narrower
Radius) and gentler by removing one. A rung may name an Archetype (Stalker, Lunger, Spitter,
Ambusher, or a pack's own id under Server/KweebecNightmare/Hunters) to fix what rises instead
of taking the roster's weighted pick. Beside the two factors above, the library's own readings
answer a ZigFactor sensor here too: ziggfreedcommon:encounter_members,
encounter_elapsed_seconds, encounter_waves, encounter_phase_index and encounter_deaths.
The SignalWorldEvent beat after each wave (zc:wave:corruption, zc:wave:shrine) lets the library
count the waves and fire its signal event; it announces nothing to a player. The script never
sends zc:engaged, binds no boss and shows no bar: it is a silent director, which is why its
binding row, Server/ZiggfreedCommon/Encounters/KweebecNightmare_Hunters.json, carries only the
Enabled switch. The Player sensor keeps the party on the encounter's roster so /zigencounter
inspect reads sensibly; the wave size reads the round's party, not this roster. No
CleanupOnRemove is authored on purpose: the round's own teardown removes every hunter, and this
entity owns none of them.
Override this file by id from your own pack to change the escalation for every server. Keep
the file name distinct from every NPC role's: an encounter script and a role share one id
namespace, and a script named after a role replaces that role at load.
